title: SA/40/2013 of ANITA Vs SHYAM SUNDAR BATRA

paras.text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Second Appeal No. 40/2013
 Anita D/o late Sri Ram Lal - Appellant
 Versus
 Shyam Sunder Batra S/o late Sri Ram Lal - Respondent
 Sri Siddharth Sah holding brief of Sri K.S. Verma, Advocate for appellant
 Sri Piyush Garg, Advocate for the respodnet.
Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral)
This second appeal is directed against the judgment and decree
dated 15-12-2012 passed by 3rd Addl. District Judge Dehradun, in
Civil Appeal No. 139/2011, Anita Vs. Shyam Sunder Batra as well as
judgment and decree dated 9-11-2011, passed by Civil Judge (J.D.) 4th
Dehradun in O.S. No. 369 of 2008, Shyam Sunder Batra vs. Anita.
 Briefly stated the facts giving rise to this appeal are that
respondent/plaintiff instituted a suit for damages and for eviction and
possession of the property in dispute, on the ground that the
defendant-appellant was permitted to stay temporarily in the property
in dispute, which was given to her in the year 2006 on the assurance
that when it is needed by the plaintiff then she will vacate the
premises and give vacant possession. As per plaint averment the
property in dispute was purchased by the plaintiff from Sri Ram Lal
S/o Sri Topan Dass by way of registered sale-deed dated 9-3-1995. It
was specifically pleaded in para-2 of the plaint that part of the
property measuring 18 feet x 30 feet was also sold out to defendant.
Thereafter plaintiff sold a part of disputed property, measuring 23
feet x 10 feet, to Baljit Singh S/o Sardhar Mohinder Singh by way
registered sale-deed dated 26-7-2002. By way of notice dated 31-5-
2008 the permission was revoked but despite of the period mentioned
in the notice i.e. 30 days, no possession was given therefore suit was
filed.

2
 The suit was contested by the defendant-appellant by filing
written statement. The defendant denied the title of plaintiff and it was
pleaded that the sale-deed was obtained by the plaintiff playing fraud
on the vendor father. In para-19 of the W.S. it was pleaded that the
sale-deed was obtained fraudulently by the plaintiff from his father
and has not paid any consideration for it.
 The court on the basis of pleadings of parties framed necessary
issues in the suit and parties adduced evidence. The trial court decreed
the suit on the ground that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit
property on the basis of registered sale deed dated 9-3-1995, executed
by his father in his favour. Apart from this the learned trial court also
gave a finding that no suit for cancellation sale-deed executed in
favour of plaintiff, has been filed either by the defendant or by the
father of parties. Therefore the defendant failed to establish her right
against the plaintiff.
 Against the decree passed by trial court, first appeal was
preferred by the defendant. The first appellate court after hearing the
parties and considering the evidence on record gave a categorical
finding that since no suit was filed for cancellation of the sale-deed
and the defendant herself purchased a part of the property assailing
the sale deed valid, the appeal was dismissed.
 Aggrieved further the defendant-appellant has preferred this
appeal and following substantial questions of law were framed in the
memo of appeal-A- Whether the sale-deed in favour of plaintiff/respondent being
based on fraud and cheating create any right in his favour and
thereby divesting defendant/appellant of her share in ancestral
property?.
B- Whether on the strength of sale deed obtained by fraud and
cheating the plaintiff/respondent can seek eviction of the
defendant/appellant?.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
 The only issue before the court for consideration as alleged by
the defendant -appellant is whether the sale-deed in favour of
plaintiff-respondent was obtained by playing fraud upon the father of

3
plaintiff. Both the courts below on the basis of evidence gave a
finding that since the appellant-defendant had also purchased part of
the property which was purchased by way of sale deed mentioned
above, therefore she cannot say that the plaintiff was not owner of
the property and it would be estoppal and acquiescence against the
defendant-appellant.
 So far as the other part of the case that permission was granted
to the defendant-appellant to remain in the possession of property, it
has been established that she was allowed to use the accommodation
temporarily. This is a disputed question of fact and since the
appellant-defendant or the father of the parties, has never filed a suit
for cancellation of sale deed which was executed in favour of the
plaintiff, therefore, it cannot be said to be a question of law that the
sale deed was obtained by playing fraud on the father of the parties.
The sale-deed had never been challenged. It is an admitted to the
appellant that the land was sold out by the father of plaintiff to the
plaintiff. In my opinion no substantial question of law arises in the
second appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed at admission
stage.
 The appeal is dismissed at admission stage.
